FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution

on 27 January 1976, after the draft finalized by the Travel Requisites Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. 0.2 Suitcases differ in design, shape, colour and size from one manufacturer Even with a particular size and shape, the quality of the to another. material and workmanship may be different. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard, due weightage proper type of materials to be used and prevalent followed by the manufacturers in this field. Though have the sizes and dimensions of there choice, a few for their guidance. 0.4 the his are has been given to the trade practices being the users are free to sizes have been given

This standard contains clauses which call for agreement between purchaser and the supplier and which permit the purchaser to use option for selection to suit his requirements. The relevant clauses 3.2, 4.2, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.9, 5.1 and 7.1.

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960". The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

3. SHAPES AND DIMENSIONS 3.1 The shapes and dimensions of suitcases shall be according to Fig. 1 and

Table 2.

FIG. 1 DESIGNATION OF FACES, SUITCASES 3.2 The suitcases may have dimensions other than those given in this standard subject to agreement between the supplier and the purchaser. 4. MANUFACTURE, WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 4.1 The suitcases shall be soundly constructed. The lid shall be closed snugly on the body. Slide fastener may also be used for closing the lid and body of suitcases made of leathercloth and thin leather.
4

4.2 Plywood or cardboard may be used to reinforce the body and lid of suitcases made of leathercloth and thin leather as agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser. 4.3 The stitching shall be single row with 28 to 32 stitches per decimeter and of even tension. At the end of each row of stitching there shall be at least three back stitches, except where reinforcing with a rivet or suitably cross stitched. The thread ends shall be trimmed or seared. 4.4 The handle shall be of the round vickle type ( paper wound ) covered with leather or leathercloth and lock stitched across the top. The handle shall be reinforced with a flat steel strip. The ends of the flat steel strip shall loop round two D-rings attached to the ends of the handle. The handle may also be of plastics moulded and attached to the D-rings as agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser. A minimum gap of 55 mm shall be provided between the handle and the body to give a comfortable grip. 4.5 The suitcases shall be equipped with two 3-position extension locks. The locks shall be secured to the front of the suitcase with steel prongs. The prongs shall pass through corresponding holes in a metal-backing plate. The backing plate shall be covered with buffing leather or leathercloth. The type and design of lock may be provided as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 4.6 The suitcases may be flexible at top, bottom or sides as agreed to When the lid is fully open, the between the purchaser and the supplier. body shall not tilt. 4.7 The inside of the suitcases shall be lined with cotton rayon silk or leathercloth as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 4.8 Suitable feet shall be provided at the bottom of the suitcases to avoid the full ground contact. 4.9 Tie tapes, pockets and slide fasteners to close the pockets provided as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 5 may be

IS : 7954 - 1976 4.10 The mild steel components

shall be coated chromium conforming to Grade 3 of IS: 106%1968*.

over nickel

4.11 The suitcases shall be finished smooth without any sharp edges or constructional defects. There shall not be any loose thread and uneven seams. 4.12 In respect of appearance, general workmanship and finish, the suitcases shall conform to the sample previously approved by the consumer. 5. SAMPLING
5.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the procedure given in IS:2500 (Part I)-19737 shall be followed for sampling. The scale of sampling shall be corresponding to inspection level III given in Table 1 of IS:2500 (Part I)-1973t.

5.2 The sampling plan shall be corresponding to AQL of 4.0 percent given in Table 2 "Single sampling AQL plans" of IS:2500 (Part I)-1973t.
6. MARKING 6.1 Each

suitcase shall be clearly

and

permanently

marked

with the

following: a) Manufacturer's name or registered trade-mark, and

b) Size of the suitcase. 6.1.1 Suitcases may also be marked with the IS1 Certification Mark.
NOTE- The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity Details of conditions under which a to that standard as a further safeguard. licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

also be packed as agreed to between the manufacturer
